No significant differences in subsequent food intake were found between the high-CHO and high-fat yogurts at any time interval. Also, there were no differences in ratings of hunger and fullness between the yogurts"
range: high-carbohydrate 81 % and high-fat 65 % of energy, similar energy density and protein; preload energy and the compensation figures not in the abstract; design (within or between subjects) not stated in the abstract; value from the abstract
citation: Rolls BJ, Kim S, McNelis AL, Fischman MW, Foltin RW, Moran TH 1991, Am J Physiol 260:R756-R763; doi:10.1152/ajpregu.1991.260.4.r756; pmid:2012246

parameter: satiety and CCK, GLP-1, PYY and ghrelin over 180 min after isocaloric oat-bran drinks of low against high viscosity
value: abstract: two "isocaloric (1250 kJ) 300-mL oat bran beverages with low or high viscosity (carbohydrates, 57.9 g; protein, 7.8 g; fat, 3.3 g; fiber, 10.2 g)"; "The oat bran beverage with low viscosity induced a greater postprandial increase in satiety (P = 0.048) and plasma glucose ..., cholecystokinin (P = 0.035), glucagon-like peptide 1 (P = 0.037), and peptide YY (P = 0.051) and a greater decrease in postprandial ghrelin (P = 0.009) than the beverage with high-viscosity oat bran"; gastric emptying faster after low viscosity (P = 0.034)
range: randomised order; blood at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180 min; no hormone values in the abstract; value from the abstract
population: 20 healthy normal-weight adults (16 women, 4 men; 22.6 y)
citation: Juvonen KR, Purhonen AK, Salmenkallio-Marttila M, Lähteenmäki L, Laaksonen DE, Herzig KH, Uusitupa MI, Poutanen KS, Karhunen LJ 2009, J Nutr 139:461-466; doi:10.3945/jn.108.099945; pmid:19176745

parameter: ghrelin, GLP-1, PYY and appetite over 2 h after isoenergetic meals with or without psyllium fibre and soy protein
value: abstract: five isoenergetic meals, fibre 6.2-7.6 g against psyllium-enriched 23.0 g, protein 2.6-2.8 g against 18.4-19.7 g; "Fiber-enriched meals decreased glucose, insulin, ghrelin, and PYY responses; in addition, PYY secretion was prolonged compared with the other meals"; GLP-1 "significantly suppressed after a fiber- and protein-rich meal"; "postprandial ratings of appetite were mostly similar after the test meals"
range: single-blind randomised crossover; 2 h only; meal energy not in the abstract; value from the abstract
citation: Karhunen LJ, Juvonen KR, Flander SM, Liukkonen KH, Lähteenmäki L, Siloaho M, Laaksonen DE, Herzig KH, Uusitupa MI, Poutanen KS 2010, J Nutr 140:737-744; doi:10.3945/jn.109.115436; pmid:20147463

parameter: hunger time course over 4 h after a 540 kcal solid against liquid meal replacement
value: Results and Figure 1: "Hunger immediately declined following meal consumption, reaching nadir levels 15 minutes post-prandially regardless of meal type. However, within 60 minutes after S and L ingestion, hunger began to progressively increase but remained lower at every time point in the S-MRP compared to the L (p < 0.05)"; "At 4-hour post-meal ingestion, hunger was 14 +/- 10 % higher than fasting with the L-MRP; whereas hunger remained below fasting with the S-MRP by 45 +/- 19 %"; hunger AUC 2408 (range 945-8805) against 8235 (range 2572-12892) mm x 240 min (p < 0.005)
range: randomised repeated measures; 540 +/- 28 kcal each, but not matched in composition: solid 64/15/25 % and liquid 73/18/10 % of energy from carbohydrate/protein/fat, fibre 2 against 12 g, weight 138 against 553 g (Table 2); ratings at 15, 60, 120, 180, 240 min; full text read
citation: Tieken SM, Leidy HJ, Stull AJ, Mattes RD, Schuster RA, Campbell WW 2007, Horm Metab Res 39:389-394; doi:10.1055/s-2007-976545; pmid:17533583

parameter: ghrelin and CCK over 4 h after a 540 kcal solid against liquid meal replacement
value: Results: ghrelin "declined following the consumption of both meals and reached nadir levels at 60 minutes (p < 0.02)"; with the solid "plasma ghrelin remained below baseline 4 hours after meal consumption (p < 0.05), whereas the plasma ghrelin following the L-MRP returned to baseline at 4 hours"; CCK change-from-baseline AUC "S: -1290 ... vs. L: -5528 pg/ml x 240 min ... p = 0.14" (not different)
range: randomised repeated measures; baselines differed between trials for ghrelin and CCK, so both were analysed as change from baseline; medians (range); full text read
citation: Tieken SM, Leidy HJ, Stull AJ, Mattes RD, Schuster RA, Campbell WW 2007, Horm Metab Res 39:389-394; doi:10.1055/s-2007-976545; pmid:17533583

parameter: hunger and ghrelin over 3 h after a solid against a liquefied high-protein meal matched for energy density, weight and volume
value: abstract: lunch of 15 % of daily energy requirement as steamed chicken breast, solid with 750 ml water or blended; hunger suppression "(79 +/- 3 mm and 52 +/- 10 mm; P < 0.03 at 20 min and 61 +/- 7 mm and 44 +/- 8 mm; P < 0.03 at 115 min) was higher in the solid condition"; "Glucose, insulin, and ghrelin concentration curves were similar for both conditions"
range: within-subject comparison; allocation order not stated in the abstract; value from the abstract
citation: Martens MJ, Lemmens SG, Born JM, Westerterp-Plantenga MS 2011, Obesity (Silver Spring) 19:522-527; doi:10.1038/oby.2010.258; pmid:20966901

parameter: satiety, gastric emptying and CCK peak after the same 2573 kJ meal eaten solid-liquid against homogenised
value: abstract: meal of "cooked vegetables 250 g, cheese 35 g, croutons 50 g and olive oil 25 g, total energy 2573 kJ, with water 300 ml"; homogenised "significantly more satiating (P < 0.05)"; gastric emptying "255 (SEM 11) min after HM v. 214 (SEM 12) min after SM; P < 0.05"; "CCK peak occurred later (94 (SEM 12) min after HM v. 62 (SEM 11) min after SM; NS)"
range: randomised order; n = 8; antral area related to fullness (r2 0.46); value from the abstract
citation: Santangelo A, Peracchi M, Conte D, Fraquelli M, Porrini M 1998, Br J Nutr 80:521-527; doi:10.1017/s0007114598001615; pmid:10211050

parameter: CCK and fullness over 4 h after isoenergetic isovolumic milk-protein products as a liquid, a viscous liquid and a gel
value: abstract: whey (low-viscous liquid), casein (high-viscous liquid) or cross-linked casein (rigid gel); "The increase in CCK was similar for Cas and Wh in the first 15 min, whereas for Cas-TG, the CCK release was significantly lower, but more sustained. The feeling of fullness was stronger after the consumption of Cas-TG than after the consumption of Cas and Wh"
range: randomised order; n = 8; energy not in the abstract; value from the abstract
citation: Juvonen KR, Karhunen LJ, Vuori E, Lille ME, Karhu T, Jurado-Acosta A, Laaksonen DE, Mykkänen HM, Niskanen LK, Poutanen KS, Herzig KH 2011, Br J Nutr 106:1890-1898; doi:10.1017/s0007114511002522; pmid:21736770
